title: Microcheckpointing and inflight kernel-swap for stable multi-stream decode
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem statement: In our multi-stream decode path we occasionally observe non-deterministic CUDA graph capture failures and subtle state divergence when we switch kernel implementations mid-prefill/decode (for example when a late kernel selector chooses a quantized or fused-attention kernel after prefill). These failures cause increased request tail latency (retries) and rare incorrect outputs due to KV-cache desynchronization.

Goals:
- Add a low-overhead, per-stream microcheckpoint mechanism that snapshots the minimal deterministic state required to safely swap kernels or to recover from a failed graph recapture.
- Ensure kernel swaps are idempotent and can be rolled back without leaking partial state to other streams.
- Reduce capture/replay failure rate by >5x and keep 99th-percentile token latency regression under 5% for typical workloads.
- Provide observable signals (metrics/traces) to correlate kernel swaps with errors and latencies.

Constraints and considerations:
- Must be compatible with existing CUDA graph capture/replay flow and not increase steady-state CPU/GPU overhead materially (goal: <1.5% extra token cost).
- Microcheckpoints must be compact: only KV-cache pointers, sequence epoch, RNG counter, and minimal allocator fences. Full tensor copies are unacceptable.
- Need graceful fallback when the GPU driver prohibits multi-graph capture or when memory fragmentation prevents an atomic swap.
- Work must be roll-outable behind a feature flag and gate-enabled per-customer for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Design proposal (high level):
1) Microcheckpoint snapshot: at prefill boundary and at kernel-handoff points create an incremental checkpoint object containing: sequence_id, prefill_len, KV-index-epoch, small control-plane nonce, and a tight checksum of last-token logits metadata. This object is persisted in an in-memory, per-stream compact store (not device-host copies).
2) Kernel-swap API: expose runtime API kernel_selector.begin_swap(stream_id) -> returns checkpoint_token. Kernel implementations must implement kernel_selector.commit_swap(checkpoint_token) and kernel_selector.rollback(checkpoint_token). commit_swap applies new kernel binding atomically; rollback restores stream-level control metadata using the microcheckpoint.
3) Idempotent recapture: when a CUDA graph recapture fails, the recapture flow will use the latest checkpoint to reconstruct the minimal deterministic state and attempt a secondary recapture using an alternative kernel selection or single-stream fallback.
4) Epoching & fencing: introduce an epoch counter per-stream; each microcheckpoint has an epoch. Swap/recapture actions are only allowed when epoch token matches to prevent TOCTOU across concurrent operations.
5) Observability: emit metrics: checkpoint_create_time_ms, checkpoint_size_bytes, swap_attempts, swap_success, recapture_attempts, recapture_success, swap_rollback_count. Trace spans link to request id and kernel variant chosen.

Trade-offs and alternatives considered:
- Full-state host-side copy (rejected): too expensive in memory and time for high-qps workloads.
- Locking heavy-handed global barriers (rejected): would serialize throughput. Instead we favor per-stream fencing and optimistic swaps with rollback.
- Avoiding any checkpointing (status quo): leads to opaque failures and higher tail latencies.

Testing & validation plan:
- Unit tests: kernel_selector API unit tests, epoch mismatch tests, rollback determinism tests.
- Integration: end-to-end multi-stream decode harness with synthetic traffic to validate correctness across quantized/fp16/fused-attention kernels.
- Fault injection: simulate driver preemption, memory allocation failures, and induced capture failures; verify that rollback recovers and that no cross-stream leakage occurs.
- Performance: measure steady-state throughput and token cost with feature enabled for M=512 prompt length distribution; aim for <1.5% CPU overhead and <5% 99p latency impact.
- Canary: staged rollout to Dedicated pool with feature flag and telemetry checks for 24h before global enable.

Acceptance criteria:
- Capture failure rate reduces by at least 5x on the internal corpus of long-prefill workloads.
- No observed KV-cache divergence in fuzzed end-to-end harness across 100k synthetic sequences.
- Metric emissions for swap_rollback_count and recapture_success are available in Console and dashboards.
- Canary shows <3% throughput regression and <5% P99 latency delta.
- Documentation (confluence) and an RFC are published and linked.

Implementation tasks (tentative):
- Runtime: add microcheckpoint store, epoching, kernel_selector API (core) (Jonas) (3 days)
- Kernel teams: add commit/rollback hooks in kernel ABI shims (2 days)
- Capture/replay: integrate checkpoint use in recapture path and recapture fallback policies (2 days)
- Tests: unit + integration harness updates and fault-injection scenarios (3 days)
- Observability: metrics/tracing + dashboard (1 day)
- Docs & rollout: RFC + Confluence + canary plan (1 day)

Artifacts and references:
- RFC draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Microcheckpoints+for+Kernel+Swap (draft)
- Design notes: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b_microcheckpoint_design (internal)
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2425 (WIP)
